comparator.name: Cybersecurity & Cybercrime
comparator.sourceNotes: The live Leiden Study Guide confirms a current 180-EC, three-year Dutch-language bachelor that started in September 2025 and integrates computer science, cybersecurity governance, law and criminology. It publishes Years 1 and 2 in full: eleven compulsory modules in each year totalling 60 EC per year. The same official product explicitly states that, because the programme is new, only first- and second-year courses appear in the 2026-2027 guide and Year 3 courses will become visible from June 2027. Only the supported 120 EC are retained; the unpublished third-year curriculum is not inferred.

exception.reason: Leiden's Cybersecurity & Cybercrime bachelor began in September 2025. The current 2026-2027 Study Guide establishes Years 1 and 2, but explicitly says that Year 3 courses will only become visible from June 2027. A complete coherent 180-EC pathway therefore cannot yet be reconstructed from current official evidence. Inferring the remaining 60 EC would invent the programme's advanced technical, governance, legal, criminological, project, elective and possible thesis requirements.
exception.curriculumContext: The supported curriculum totals 120 EC: a 60-EC first year combining programming, systems and networks, cybersecurity governance, criminology, law, organisational security, research and skills labs with an integrated disinformation project; and a 60-EC second year combining cyber offenders and victims, criminal law, cyber conflict, crisis response, technical attacks and defence, investigation, quantitative and qualitative methods, and an integrated ransomware project. The official product confirms that the bachelor as a whole is 180 EC, but the final 60 EC are not yet published.
